warning: These are SYNTHETIC report fixtures — NOT observations of real domains. They must never be read as, merged with, or cited as real-domain data. No real company is described here.
purpose: Calibrate the accumulation-Red threshold AND its denominator (Story 18 §3.4 / §5). Real domains with 3+ concurrent soft flags and no threat listing did not occur in the 18.2 corpus — the maximum observed was 2 concurrent hygiene flags (or 3 counting young-domain age on v0.dev). Owner pre-approved synthetics for this range.
caveat: The accumulation threshold set against these fixtures MUST be re-validated against real domains when any turn up. A threshold calibrated only on synthetic data is provisional. Only no_dmarc, no_spf and young_domain are grounded in observed co-occurrence (v0.dev, gutenberg.org, catb.org, ccc.de); flags beyond those are real signal TYPES the collectors produce but were not observed stacked this high in the corpus, so their co-occurrence is extrapolated and flagged per fixture.
denominator_note: Story 18 §5 recommends the accumulation ratio be findings / SUCCESSFULLY-CHECKED signals (not attempted), with a minimum-checks floor. Fixtures vary checks_succeeded so Story 19 can exercise that ratio. A full report attempts ~12 checks: domain_age, dmarc, spf, mx, hosting, wayback_depth, ai_pivot, cert_history, phishtank, urlhaus, trustpilot, bbb.

flag_vocabulary.no_dmarc: OBSERVED in corpus (masshist.org, suckless.org, slackware.com, xfce.org, bun.sh, gutenberg.org, catb.org, ccc.de, v0.dev)
flag_vocabulary.no_spf: OBSERVED in corpus (gutenberg.org, catb.org, ccc.de, deepsprings.edu, v0.dev)
flag_vocabulary.thin_archive: real signal type (low Wayback capture count); NOT observed stacked with hygiene flags — 18.2's young domains had healthy archives — so co-occurrence is EXTRAPOLATED
flag_vocabulary.whois_privacy: real signal type (RDAP/WHOIS registrant privacy); not extracted in 18.2 — EXTRAPOLATED
flag_vocabulary.no_reputation: real signal type (no Trustpilot/BBB presence); reputation collector not run in 18.2 — EXTRAPOLATED
flag_vocabulary.no_mx: real signal type (no DNS MX); all 18.2 corpus domains had MX — EXTRAPOLATED (plausible for a non-email site)

fixtures.derived_from: v0.dev — this exact triple (young ~2.9y + no DMARC + no SPF) was OBSERVED together in the corpus. Fully realistic.
the v0.dev triple + thin_archive. In the corpus young domains were NOT thin (v0.dev had 401 captures), so young+thin co-occurrence is extrapolated but plausible for a hastily-stood-up site.

same 4 flags as synth-acc-4, but with a DEGRADED denominator — cert_history, phishtank and urlhaus checks failed. Included specifically to exercise the §5 ratio: 4/8 (0.50) here vs 4/12 (0.33) in synth-acc-4, same findings.
fixtures.grounding: 3 observed + 1 extrapolated; denominator degraded (mirrors the real crt.sh + no-threat-key gaps seen in 18.2)

fixtures.derived_from: the 4-flag set + whois_privacy. WHOIS privacy on a young domain is a named draft signal (mvp-spec §2E draft) though not extracted in 18.2 — extrapolated.
the 5-flag set + no_reputation (no Trustpilot/BBB). Reputation was not collected in 18.2 — extrapolated. Denominator degraded by the (real) crt.sh outage.
the 6-flag set + no_mx. An extreme stack — deliberately at the high end to bracket the threshold. Several flags extrapolated; least realistic fixture, use only to bound the top end.
fixtures.grounding: 3 observed + 4 extrapolated — HIGHEST extrapolation, treat as an upper bracket only
